absent: Security decision criteria for pre-read and post-read hooks and the meaning of read identity values.
Full structure layouts, field offsets and sizes for nodes, roots, super info and attribute objects.
Complete lock ordering, sleepable versus atomic contexts and interrupt safety across all locks.
Activation, deactivation, removal and rename transitions beyond the observed reference checks.
Behavior of allocation, reference counting, hashing, string copy and balanced tree helpers.
Concurrent mutation handling during path building, lookup and revalidation windows.
Semantics of revision counters, identifier allocation and generation reuse for cache coherence.
File, directory and link operation tables and address space behavior for input-output paths.

findings.text: The helper kernel_read_file provides the central in-kernel file content contract. It serves only regular files, rejects offset and buffer combinations that cannot be satisfied, bounds length to a positive sane range, holds write denial across the operation, asks a pre-read security authority with a whole-file flag, optionally reports total size, allocates backing storage when the caller passes an empty slot, repeatedly requests bytes until capacity is filled or data ends, requires exact consumption plus a post-read security approval for whole-file reads, discards internal storage on failure, always releases write denial, and reports copied length or a negative failure.

The helpers kernel_read_file_from_path and kernel_read_file_from_path_initns and kernel_read_file_from_fd adapt the core contract to different handles. The path variants reject empty names, open read-only, delegate, then release the reference, with the initns variant performing the open under the initial filesystem context. The descriptor variant scopes the numeric handle, rejects missing entries or handles lacking read mode, then delegates using the underlying file object.

Whole-file status holds exactly when reading from the start with capacity covering total size. That status drives both the pre-read decision input and the later requirement for exact consumption plus post-read approval. Oversize inputs beyond the signed maximum, empty or negative sizes, and whole-file requests without size reporting but insufficient capacity are all rejected. Partial reads may stop early at end of data without post validation.

The helpers kernfs_name and kernfs_path_from_node plus the locked builder expose hierarchy naming. The single-name query handles absent nodes with a placeholder and parentless nodes as root. The full-path query defaults a missing origin to the hierarchy root, short-circuits identical endpoints to root, otherwise delegates to the locked composer that emits parent traversals for the origin side followed by slash-separated child names toward the target.

The naming path holds read-side protection throughout, and additionally holds the hierarchy rename read lock when the target root allows parent mutation. Parent acquisition for reference counting also occurs under that rename read lock. The two print continuation helpers serialize a single shared bounded buffer with an interrupt-saving spinlock, and the multi-component walk reuses that same buffer under the same spinlock while splitting and resolving each element.

Depth counts parent links from a descendant up toward but excluding a stipulated ancestor using protected traversal. Common ancestor search requires both nodes to share one hierarchy root, lifts the deeper side to equal depth, then climbs both sides together until they meet, with the root as guaranteed convergence.

Namespace identity is numeric with zero denoting absence. Enablement is build dependent: one variant reports the per-node namespace flag while an alternate variant reports always disabled. The root flag accessor simply forwards the owning hierarchy flag word.

Child ordering derives from a namespace-seeded string hash reduced to a bounded positive range with small and extreme values reserved, followed by namespace identifier comparison and finally lexical name comparison. The sibling comparator applies that triple to two nodes by extracting the left name and namespace under protection.

Sibling linkage inserts into a per-directory balanced tree ordered by the triple comparison, rejecting duplicates. Successful insertion updates directory sub-object accounting and revision under the hierarchy attribute write lock.

The hierarchy structural semaphore guards mutation and lookup. Addition holds the write side, while name-based find and walk wrappers hold the read side. Internal find expects appropriate holding depending on context, and directory timestamp updates plus sub-directory accounting nest the attribute write lock inside the structural lock. Revalidation and lookup also hold the read side while checking activity, parent stability, naming, namespace and revision.

Addition validates namespace presence against parent requirement, requires a directory parent that is neither being removed nor marked empty, computes the ordering hash, links the sibling, refreshes parent timestamps, releases structural protection, then activates for user visibility unless the hierarchy requests deactivated creation. Directory creation and empty-directory creation allocate a directory node, attach root, namespace and private data, then delegate to addition with cleanup on failure.

Allocation for a new node imitates ownership inheritance: when the parent carries group inheritance, the requested group may be replaced by the parent stored group and directory modes gain the inheritance bit. Actual storage allocation delegates to a lower-level constructor with hierarchy, parent, name, mode, ownership and flags.

Activity tracking uses a counter that rejects acquisition for absent nodes or nodes already in negative deactivation bias, otherwise increments and optionally records dependency. Release decrements and, only upon reaching the deactivated bias value, wakes all waiters on the hierarchy deactivation queue.

Observed hierarchy objects carry parent linkage, reference-counted names, ordering hashes, optional namespace handles, type and flag words, mode and ownership attributes, revision counters, child trees with sub-directory counts, root back pointers, private payloads, reference and active counters, reclamation heads, tree links, dependency maps, identifier values, size attributes and attribute storage, plus hierarchy roots holding structural and attribute locks, rename locks, deactivation queues and identifier tables, and super information linking back to the root and namespace.
Deferred reclamation releases the name reference, frees optional attribute storage to its cache, then returns the node itself to its cache. The container is recovered from the reclamation head.

Dentry to node binding first checks whether the filesystem operations match the hierarchy operations, then rejects truly negative entries whose inode slot is empty, otherwise follows the inode private pointer. Superblock to hierarchy translation similarly validates operations before returning the stored root, with super private data accessed through a dedicated accessor.

Persistent identifiers split differently by word size: wide inode builds fix generation to one while narrow builds carry generation in high bits. Lookup by identifier searches the hierarchy identifier table under protection, validates full inode or generation equality, requires prior activation plus a live reference, and returns with protection dropped or null on any mismatch.

Lookup resolves a child by name under hierarchy read protection using the super namespace when required, hides inactive nodes by returning no entry without negative instantiation, materializes an inode on success, stamps the parent revision onto the dentry for later negative validation, and splices the result. Revalidation rejects protected-tree lookups, discards negative entries when the parent revision moved, otherwise retains them, and for positive entries requires continued activity, stable parent linkage, unchanged name and matching namespace.

The directory dentry operations expose revalidation as the sole dentry hook, while inode lookup serves directory missing-name resolution. Revalidation acts as a gate returning retry, valid or invalid indications, and lookup acts as instantiation producing an inode or a negative marker.

Reuse of one global bounded print buffer for both diagnostic printing and path walking means concurrent users must serialize or risk corrupted output, overlong inputs are truncated with explicit diagnostic fallbacks, inactive nodes remain invisible to avoid aliasing, and namespace mismatches plus revision skew force revalidation failure rather than stale reuse.

Ordering hashes never use the lowest two values nor the extreme signed maximum, reserving them for special directory entries. Empty directories are created with world-readable and searchable directory permissions under root ownership. Size violations report file-too-large, malformed requests report invalid argument, allocation failures report out-of-memory, short whole-file transfers report input-output error, unreadable descriptors report bad descriptor, duplicate names report already exists, missing parents report no entry, and protected-tree revalidation requests a retry.

The helpers kernfs_get_parent and kernfs_find_and_get_node_by_id and kernfs_find_and_get_ns and kernfs_walk_and_get_ns and kernfs_get_inode and kernfs_root_flags and kernfs_root_from_sb provide reference-counted access to parents, identifiers, names, paths, inodes and hierarchy metadata. Single-name and multi-component searches acquire read protection, resolve, then hold a reference before releasing protection, returning null when absent.

Inode instantiation attaches a held node reference as private data, assigns generic address and inode operations, records generation from the identifier, applies default mode attributes and refreshes from hierarchy state, then specializes by node type for directories, regular files and links, with empty directories further marked empty, before unlocking the new inode.
